feature: West German 1970 national programme rewards and Energy Mix modifier unit correction
scope: 54 existing GER focus nodes. No focus ID, layout, time, prerequisite, exclusion, leader, RAF/security system, sandbox mechanic, DDR rivalry or history record changed. Party-bound incremental programmes have explicit visible ruling-party requirements and permanent receipt flags.
route_cost_note: All route currency figures freeze GDP at the scenario start of 216.629bn for comparison. Runtime charges recalculate against GDP when each focus completes, so later nominal amounts can differ. Ratios sum one-time GDP fractions, with pre-existing treasury costs and revenue identified separately. These are coherent example paths, not every possible tech or focus sequence.

gating.availability: Existing party/coalition requirements remain. Added BAföG and Works Constitution requirements use western_social_democrats_are_in_power = yes; Barzel social market uses western_conservatism_are_in_power = yes. These native MD requirements display the current party names and remain visible while unavailable. Current CHP/Green federal government logic remains for Eco-Tax and Atomkonsens. Named-state owner/control, real building cap and amount-aware specialty tech cap remain visible.
gating.execution: The original completion reward and new package run inside the same one-time guarded transaction. It checks original effective availability, GER tag, 1970 scenario, GDP > 0, full coalesced site/capacity/technology requirements, and a focus-specific permanent receipt; no partial package and no replay after return to a previous government.
gating.slots: Every added building level gets one shared slot before construction. An AST walk adds any missing slots to the original fixed-state rewards within the selected 54 focus nodes; whole-payout capacity gates coalesce original and added building levels.
gating.native_capacity: tools/german_reward_revision_20261027/programme_assets.py reads current MD building state_max and enable_building levels. Specialized reactor, renewable, and microchip packages use amount-aware technology tiers; dockyards require a coastal site.
gating.costs: New one-time charges use cw_lib.money_gdp as GDP fractions; no new recurring stream or treasury affordability requirement. No free reactors, renewables, microchip plant, or uranium production.
gating.energy_unit_fix: Existing Energie core values are previewed as percentages but were linked to flat fossil_fuel_consumption and nuclear_energy_gain modifiers. The GER-only mapping is corrected to fossil_pp_fuel_consumption_modifier and nuclear_energy_generation_modifier; player-facing percentages now match modifier scale. Only this GER block is patched in the dynamic-modifier output.

stimulus_versus_austerity.existing_tradeoff: Original focus still adds debt on stimulus and raises treasury on austerity.

nuclear_expansion_versus_moratorium.description: Kalkar/Hamm reactor investment versus renewable development in Schleswig-Holstein, both following the initial reactor buildout.

W15_versus_W18.description: No new conscription factor added by the overlay. Offers readiness, limited-use research and procurement savings.

SPD_stimulus_and_high_technology.note: The 4.2% gross treasury outlay is 3.2% from new packages plus existing BAföG, pension, steel and Ruhr costs. The focus path also adds existing debt of 0.6% GDP. Enabling foci are shown but do not have overlay packages.

SPD_austerity_and_high_technology.note: Gross charges are 4.0% GDP. Existing austerity revenue offsets 0.4% GDP, leaving an illustrative 3.6% net cash outlay.

original_reward_slot_repairs.method: AST walk of numeric state scopes in each selected original reward. The transaction adds exactly the missing shared slot count before fixed-state construction, including types that do not normally consume shared slots. Existing sufficient slot grants are retained.
